ex.en: Life expectancy has risen sharply thanks to better medical care.
ex.zh: 由于医疗条件改善，预期寿命大幅提高。

ex.en: There was an air of expectancy in the hall before the results were announced.
ex.zh: 结果宣布之前，大厅里弥漫着期待的气氛。

ex.en: Doctors say early treatment can add years to a patient's life expectancy.
ex.zh: 医生说，早期治疗可以延长病人多年的预期寿命。

senses: n. 期待，预期；期望，盼望
expectation.usage: 辨析:expectation指盼望某事发生;anticipation指基于先见的期待;hope缺根据把握;outlook据征兆预感;prospect指可能实现的愿望；n.期待，预期；期望，指望；ex（表示“往外”）+pect（看）+ation（名词后缀，表行为）→往外看的行为→期望，期待；索引p408

ex.en: She went to college with great expectations.
ex.zh: 她满怀希望地进入大学。

ex.en: The product failed to meet customers' expectation of high quality.
ex.zh: 该产品未能达到顾客对高质量的期望。

ex.en: Contrary to expectation, the new policy proved popular with most voters.
ex.zh: 与预期相反，新政策证明受到大多数选民的欢迎。

senses: n. 探险；远征；探险队，远征队
n. （为特定目的而组织的）旅行，远征
expedition.usage: [族]expeditionary a. 远征的；ex（表示往外）+pedi（发音类似“盆地”）+tion（名词后缀）→去塔里木盆地“探险”。；索引p408

ex.en: The expedition to the South Pole lasted nearly six months.
ex.zh: 这次南极探险历时近六个月。

ex.en: Scientists joined the expedition to study marine life in the deep ocean.
ex.zh: 科学家们参加了此次远征，以研究深海海洋生物。

ex.en: The expedition team carried enough supplies to survive the polar winter.
ex.zh: 探险队携带了足够的给养，以便在极地严冬中生存。

ex.en: The student was expelled for cheating in the final examination.
ex.zh: 该学生因期末考试作弊被开除。

ex.en: The government expelled two diplomats accused of spying.
ex.zh: 政府驱逐了两名被指控从事间谍活动的外交官。

ex.en: The engine expels hot gases through a narrow pipe.
ex.zh: 发动机通过一根细管排出热气。

expend.usage: 同义：spend, exhaust, waste；派生 expendable adj. 可消耗的；熟悉expensive（昂贵的）→昂贵的要花很多钱→花费

ex.en: Since 1914, scientists have known that birds flying in formation—a V-shape—expend less energy.
ex.zh: 自1914年以来，科学家们就知道鸟类以V字形飞行消耗的能量更少。

senses: n. (时间、金钱等的)支出,消耗
expenditure.usage: [族] expend vt. 花费；[近] expense n. 花费；expenditure 支出；income 收入；常搭配 on。；易混词辨析:expense强调一般的支出;expenditure强调官方的支出,多用在如“政府开支、国防开支”等正式词语中；索引p408

ex.en: The government cut public expenditure on welfare.
ex.zh: 政府削减了福利方面的公共支出。

ex.en: Household expenditure on education has risen faster than income over the past decade.
ex.zh: 过去十年，家庭教育支出的增长快于收入的增长。

ex.en: The ministry must approve any capital expenditure above one million dollars.
ex.zh: 凡超过一百万美元的资本支出均须获得该部批准。

expense.usage: at the expense of...以……为代价；n.费用；报销；开支；n.费用；开支；索引p408

ex.en: She always travels first-class regardless of expense.
ex.zh: 无论费用多高她总是乘头等舱。

ex.en: He finished the project on time, but at great expense to his health.
ex.zh: 他按时完成了项目，却付出了巨大的健康代价。

ex.en: The company will cover all the travel expenses for the training course.
ex.zh: 公司将承担培训课程的所有差旅费用。

expensive.usage: [反]cheap a. 便宜的；adj.昂贵的 日本和很多国家exchange 了意见，但eventually,还是决定把nuclear 污水排入大海。 Network 上有大量关于日本image 的negative 评论。Overall,这个phenomenon 影响是；adj.昂贵的

ex.en: Fresh vegetables are far more expensive in winter than in summer.
ex.zh: 新鲜蔬菜冬天比夏天贵得多。

ex.en: Hiring more staff is an expensive way to solve the staffing crisis.
ex.zh: 雇更多员工是解决人手危机的一种昂贵方式。

ex.en: The most expensive option is not always the most effective one.
ex.zh: 最昂贵的选择未必是最有效的。

experience.usage: undergo 的近义词；[U]经验；[C]经历

ex.en: Volunteering abroad gives young people experience that no classroom can provide.
ex.zh: 到国外做志愿服务能让年轻人获得课堂无法提供的经历。

experiment.usage: experiment on/with...对……做实验；n.实验，试验；尝试，实践 v.做试验；尝试

ex.en: The scientists repeated the experiment several times to confirm the result.
ex.zh: 科学家们多次重复该实验以确认结果。

ex.en: Schools are experimenting with later start times to improve students' performance.
ex.zh: 学校正在试行推迟上课时间，以提高学生的成绩。

ex.en: An experiment on hundreds of volunteers showed that the diet really works.
ex.zh: 一项有数百名志愿者参与的实验表明这种饮食确实有效。

ex.en: Years of experimentation were needed before the drug could be approved for public use.
ex.zh: 这种药物经过了多年实验才获准供公众使用。

expert.usage: an expert in/on...……方面的专家；辨：强调在任一领域内已经达到了一定水平，比specialist更受人尊敬；索引p408

ex.en: His expert evidence played a key role in the trial.
ex.zh: 他的专家证据在审判中起了关键作用。

ex.en: She is an expert in ancient Roman history and often advises museums.
ex.zh: 她是古罗马史专家，经常为博物馆提供咨询。

ex.en: Even an expert driver can make mistakes on icy mountain roads.
ex.zh: 在冰雪覆盖的山路上，再老到的司机也可能出错。

senses: n. 专门知识(或技能等),专长

ex.en: We have the expertise to help you run your business.
ex.zh: 我们有帮助你经营自己企业的专门知识。

ex.en: The project requires technical expertise that the current team lacks.
ex.zh: 该项目需要目前团队所缺乏的技术专长。

ex.en: Her expertise in environmental law made her the obvious choice for the case.
ex.zh: 她在环境法方面的专业知识使她成为办理此案的不二人选。

ex.en: The firm hired outside consultants to supply the missing expertise.
ex.zh: 公司聘请了外部顾问来提供所缺的专业知识。

senses: vi. 满期,届期,(期限)终止
v. 期满，届满；去世；失效，终止
vi. (正式文件)到期；过期；失效

ex.en: My passport expires next March, so I need to renew it soon.
ex.zh: 我的护照明年三月到期，所以需要尽快换发。

ex.en: The lease expires at the end of the year, and rents are expected to rise.
ex.zh: 租约年底到期，预计租金将会上涨。

ex.en: If the offer is not accepted within thirty days, it will expire.
ex.zh: 如果三十天内未被接受，该要约即告失效。

explain.usage: clarify 的近义词；[族]explanation n. 解释；索引p408

ex.en: The professor explained the theory with a simple diagram on the whiteboard.
ex.zh: 教授用白板上的一幅简单图示讲解了这个理论。

ex.en: In her letter she explained why she had to decline the offer.
ex.zh: 她在信中解释了不得不拒绝该邀请的原因。

ex.en: Economists struggle to explain the sudden rise in housing prices.
ex.zh: 经济学家难以解释房价的突然上涨。

senses: adj. 可说明的；可解释的

ex.en: Most of the apparent anomalies in the data are explainable once seasonal factors are taken into account.
ex.zh: 一旦把季节因素考虑在内，数据中大多数表面上的异常都是可以解释的。

ex.en: There is no simple explanation for why some languages survive and others die out.
ex.zh: 对于为什么有些语言存续而有些消亡，并没有简单的解释。

ex.en: His explanation for being late did not convince the manager.
ex.zh: 他对迟到所做的解释未能让经理信服。

ex.en: The most likely explanation is that the sample was too small.
ex.zh: 最可能的解释是样本太小。

ex.en: The footnotes serve an explicatory purpose, clarifying terms that general readers may not know.
ex.zh: 这些脚注起阐释作用，澄清普通读者可能不熟悉的术语。

senses: adj. 明确的，清楚的；坦率的
adj. 明确的；直言不讳的
explicit.usage: [反]implicit a. 含蓄的；同义：clear, definite, specific, direct；反义：implicit；adj.清楚的，明确的；直截 了当的；ex(外,出)+pli(发音似"铺里")+c(发音似see"看见")+it(它)→展示给大家看清→清楚的；索引p408

ex.en: She was quite explicit about why she had left.
ex.zh: 她对自己离开的原因直言不讳。

ex.en: It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
ex.zh: 国会需要一劳永逸地赋予委员会明确的权力，禁止宽带供应商干涉其网络访问量，并制定明确的规则，保护网络的开放性和创新性。

ex.en: The teacher gave explicit instructions on how to carry out the science experiment.
ex.zh: 老师就如何进行科学实验给出了明确的指示。

explicitly.usage: adv.清楚明确地；直截了 当地，坦率地；露骨地， 不隐晦地；索引p408

ex.en: The manual explicitly warns users not to disassemble the device while it is charging.
ex.zh: 说明书明确警告用户不要在设备充电时将其拆开。

explode.usage: [族]explosion n. 爆炸；[族] exploded a. 分解的；[近] burst vt.&vi.（使）爆炸；ex（出）+plod（爆裂；大声音）+e→爆炸。；索引p408

ex.en: More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
ex.zh: 最近，人们对益生菌食品和植物性肉类也有类似的质疑，但如今这两种产品都迅速成为超市的主要产品。

ex.en: The tank exploded, shaking buildings several streets away.
ex.zh: 油罐爆炸了，几条街外的建筑物都为之震动。

ex.en: The city's population has exploded since the new subway opened.
ex.zh: 自新地铁开通以来，这座城市的人口激增。

ex.en: The manual includes an exploded diagram showing how the engine's components fit together.
ex.zh: 说明书里附有一张分解图，展示发动机各部件如何组装在一起。

senses: n. 英勇的或冒险的行为或事迹
vt. 开发,开采,开拓;利用

phrases.m: adj. 可利用的,可开发的

exploit.usage: [族]exploitation n. 剥削；同义①explore②utilize；explo（联想成explore“探索”）+it（它）→我们探索它是为了“利用、开发”它的资源。；词根记忆: ex(out, 出)+plo(fold, 折叠)+it→折叠再利用→利用；索引p408

ex.en: While traditional "paid" media—such as television commercials and print advertisements—still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media.
ex.zh: 虽然传统的“付费”媒介——比如电视广告和平面广告——仍然扮演着重要的角色，但如今企业还可以利用许多非传统形式的媒介。

ex.en: The firm was accused of exploiting its workers by paying them very low wages.
ex.zh: 该公司被指控以极低的工资剥削工人。

ex.en: Engineers found a way to exploit solar energy in remote mountain villages.
ex.zh: 工程师们找到了在偏远山村利用太阳能的方法。

exploitation.usage: n.剥削；开发，开采；利用；索引p408

ex.en: The report exposes the exploitation of migrant workers in the construction industry.
ex.zh: 报告揭露了建筑业中移民工人受剥削的情况。

ex.en: Sensible exploitation of natural resources can support economic growth without lasting damage.
ex.zh: 合理开发利用自然资源可以支撑经济增长而不造成持久破坏。

ex.en: Unions were formed to protect workers from exploitation by factory owners.
ex.zh: 工会的成立是为了保护工人免受工厂主的剥削。

ex.en: Space exploration demands huge investment and long-term international cooperation.
ex.zh: 太空探索需要巨额投资和长期的国际合作。

ex.en: The book traces the exploration of the Amazon from the sixteenth century onward.
ex.zh: 这本书追溯了自十六世纪以来对亚马逊地区的探索历程。

ex.en: A full exploration of the causes of the crisis lies beyond this report.
ex.zh: 对危机成因的全面探究超出了本报告的范围。

phrases.m: n. 探险者,考察者,勘探者

explore.usage: [族]exploration n. 探索；同义①look at②research；v.探讨，探究；考察，探索；单词发音类似“一丝不落”→地质学家正在一丝不落地“勘查”这个地方。；词根记忆:ex(out,向外)+plor(weep,大叫,哭喊)+e→原指猎人在打猎时通过大叫把鸟赶出山林→探索；索引p408

ex.en: Specific brain regions that respond during direct gaze are being explored by other researches, using advanced methods of brain scanning.
ex.zh: 其他研究人员正在利用各种先进的脑部扫描技术，对在眼神交流中做出反应的特定脑部区域进行研究。

ex.en: The report explores the causes of rising house prices in large cities.
ex.zh: 该报告探讨了大城市房价上涨的原因。

ex.en: Columbus and other sailors explored unknown seas in search of new trade routes.
ex.zh: 哥伦布和其他水手为寻找新的贸易航线而探索未知海域。

senses: n. [C] 探险者；勘探者；考察者

ex.en: The explorer kept a detailed diary of his journey across the desert.
ex.zh: 这位探险家详细记录了他穿越沙漠的旅程。

ex.en: Early explorers risked their lives to map unknown coastlines.
ex.zh: 早期探险家冒着生命危险绘制未知海岸线的地图。

ex.en: Modern deep-sea explorers use robots to reach the ocean floor.
ex.zh: 现代深海探险家利用机器人到达海底。

explosion.usage: explode的名词形式；词根记忆: ex(out, 出)+plos(strike, 打，击)+ion(名词后缀)→被打后情绪爆发→(感情，尤指愤怒的)迸发；索引p408

ex.en: But that very anonymity is also behind the explosion of cyber-crime that has swept across the Web.
ex.zh: 但正是这种匿名的方式导致了已席卷整个互联网的网络犯罪的激增。

ex.en: The explosion at the chemical plant injured more than twenty workers.
ex.zh: 化工厂的爆炸造成二十多名工人受伤。

ex.en: There has been an explosion of interest in electric vehicles in recent years.
ex.zh: 近年来，人们对电动汽车的兴趣激增。

senses: a. 突增的；易爆炸的；暴躁的
adj. 爆炸(性)的,爆发(性)的

ex.en: The police found no explosive devices inside the building.
ex.zh: 警方在大楼内没有发现爆炸装置。

ex.en: Immigration remains an explosive political issue in many European countries.
ex.zh: 在许多欧洲国家，移民仍是一个极易引发争议的政治问题。

ex.en: The region has seen explosive growth in online shopping in recent years.
ex.zh: 近年来该地区的网络购物出现了爆炸式增长。

export.usage: [反]import vt. 进口；词根记忆：ex(out,向外)+port(carry,携带)→带到国境外→出口。；索引p408

ex.en: Our other education related exports earn up to £10 billion a year.
ex.zh: 其他与教育相关的出口收入每年更是高达100亿英镑。

ex.en: The country exports most of its coffee to Europe and North America.
ex.zh: 该国把大部分咖啡出口到欧洲和北美。

ex.en: Textiles remain the leading export of the region despite rising labor costs.
ex.zh: 尽管劳动力成本上升，纺织品仍是该地区的主要出口产品。

senses: vt. 使暴露于（尤指危险）
expose.usage: ex-(外)+pos(放)→放到外面→暴露；[族] exposure n. 暴露；接触；[反] 掩藏；be exposed to...接触……；v.暴露，使显露；使遭受； 揭露；ex(表示"往外")+pose(姿势，摆姿势)→往外摆姿势，往外放→(使)暴露，曝光；expose...to... 使暴露于/接触；expos

ex.en: My job as a journalist is to expose the truth.
ex.zh: 我作为记者的职责就是揭露真相。

ex.en: Children should be exposed to good music.
ex.zh: 应该让孩子们接触优秀的音乐。

ex.en: In a series of four experiments, behavioral scientists at the University of Chicago and the Wisconsin School of Business tested students' willingness to expose themselves to unpleasant stimuli in an effort to satisfy curiosity.
ex.zh: 在一系列的四次试验中，芝加哥大学和威斯康星商学院的行为科学家测试了学生为了满足好奇心而让自己体验不舒服的刺激的意愿。

senses: n. (to)受到,面临,遭受(危险或不快)
n. 暴露；揭发；亮相；面临，遭受
exposure.usage: expose的名词形式；n.暴露，接触；曝光，揭 发；词根记忆：ex+pos+ure→放在外面的结果→曝光；②接触(2018完形)；索引p408

ex.en: The report recommends people to avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight.
ex.zh: 报告建议人们应避免晒太阳时间过长。

ex.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long.
ex.zh: 在19世纪40年代到50年代，在摄影技术早期，曝光时间特别长。

ex.en: Regular exposure to a second language helps young children learn it more naturally.
ex.zh: 经常接触第二语言有助于幼儿更自然地学习它。

senses: vt. 表达；表示；表现；描绘
express.usage: [族]expression n. 表达；v.表达；表现，体现 n.快车；快递 adj.快递的，特快的；明确的；v.表达；表现 n.快车；快递 adj.快递的；ex(向外)+press(压)→把压在心里的事情表达出来→表达；索引p408

ex.en: Customers expressed interest in trying the product.
ex.zh: 顾客表示有兴趣试用该产品。

ex.en: In the former case the education is incidental; it is natural and important, but it is not the express reason of the association.
ex.zh: 在前一种情况下，教育是偶然发生的，虽说这种教育很自然也很重要，但却不是这种联系存在的明确原因。

ex.en: Many young people find it easier to express their feelings online than face to face.
ex.zh: 许多年轻人发现，在网上表达情感比面对面更容易。

phrases.p: verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need
phrases.m: 通过语言或者非语言所表达出来的情感需求

expression.usage: beyond expression难以言表；n.表达；表情，神情；措词；n.表达；表情，神情；说法；索引p408

ex.en: There was a sad expression on her face as she read the letter.
ex.zh: 读信时，她脸上有一种悲伤的表情。

ex.en: The expression "a piece of cake" means something very easy to do.
ex.zh: "a piece of cake（小菜一碟）"这个短语的意思是非常容易做到的事。

ex.en: Freedom of expression is protected by law in many democratic countries.
ex.zh: 在许多民主国家，表达自由受法律保护。

expressive.usage: adj.富于表现力的；表达的；adj.富于表现力的；表现的；索引p408

ex.en: The dancer's expressive gestures conveyed emotions that words could hardly describe.
ex.zh: 舞者富有表现力的手势传达了言语难以描述的情感。

ex.en: The contract expressly states that either party may terminate the agreement with three months' written notice.
ex.zh: 合同明确规定，任何一方均可提前三个月书面通知终止协议。

senses: adj. 精美的，精致的；剧烈的
adj. 感觉强烈的,剧烈的
adj. 精致的，高雅的；敏锐的；剧烈的
exquisite.usage: 派生 exquisitely adv. 精巧地,敏锐地；exquisiteness n. 精致,细腻

ex.en: Parents don't have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance.
ex.zh: 父母不需敏锐到每时每刻都在孩子身边，但需要有一种平衡。

ex.en: The palace is decorated with exquisite carvings and hand-painted tiles.
ex.zh: 宫殿里装饰着精美的雕刻和手绘瓷砖。

ex.en: The manuscript survives in exquisite condition despite its age.
ex.zh: 尽管年代久远，这份手稿仍保存得极为完好。

ex.en: She felt exquisite embarrassment when her mistake was pointed out in public.
ex.zh: 当众被指出错误时，她感到极度难堪。

ex.en: The ancient carvings are exquisitely detailed, reflecting the remarkable skill of their makers.
ex.zh: 这些古代雕刻细节精致入微，反映出制作者高超的技艺。

extend.usage: prolong 的近义词；[族]extension n. 延长；ex（出，外）+tend（伸展）→向外伸展→延长，伸展。；词根:ex(out向外)+tend(stretch伸展)→向外伸展→扩大…的范围;③vi.包括(2021年翻译):And the demand that rose in those societie

ex.en: And the demand that rose in those societies for entry to higher education extended to groups and social classes that had not thought of attending a university before the war.
ex.zh: 这些社会中对接受高等教育的要求增加,扩大到那些在战前没有想过上大学的群体和社会阶层。

ex.en: To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
ex.zh: 为了弄清楚这是否也适用于非生物，拉蕾·奎因测试了老鼠是否能感知到机器老鼠发出的社交信号。

ex.en: And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
ex.zh: 如果萨迪克·汗获胜，并按照他的计划在2021年将它（超低排放区）延伸至南北环形公路，那么势必会引发更多将会被影响到的驾车者的强烈反对。

senses: n. 伸展，延伸；扩建部分
n. 延期；扩大；扩建部分
extension.usage: n.延伸，扩展；延期；延伸部 分；索引p408

ex.en: My home life was becoming no more than an extension of my job.
ex.zh: 我的家庭生活只不过是我工作的延伸。

ex.en: Enraged by Entergy's behavior, the Vermont Senate voted 26 to 4 last year against allowing an extension.
ex.zh: 安特吉的行为激怒了佛蒙特州参议院，去年参议院以26票对4票否决了（核电站执照）延期。

ex.en: The library applied for an extension of the loan period for rare books.
ex.zh: 图书馆申请延长珍本图书的借阅期限。

senses: adj. 广阔的，广泛的；大量的
extensive.usage: 记：ex-(向外)+tens(伸)+-ive(形后缀)→向外无限延伸的→广阔的；[族]extensively ad.广泛地；extensible a.可延长的；adj.广阔的；广泛的；大量的；索引p408

ex.en: The house has extensive grounds.
ex.zh: 这栋房子有宽敞的庭院。

ex.en: The police carried out an extensive search of the area but found no trace of the missing child.
ex.zh: 警方对该地区进行了大规模搜查，但没有找到失踪孩子的任何踪迹。

ex.en: extensive research
ex.zh: 广泛的研究

ex.en: The new drug was tested extensively on animals before it was approved for human trials.
ex.zh: 这种新药在获准进行人体试验之前，已在动物身上进行了广泛测试。

senses: n. 程度；大小，面积，范围
extent.usage: to some extent在某种程度上；n.程度；范围，长度；索引p408

ex.en: To some extent, the failure of the project was caused by poor planning.
ex.zh: 从某种程度上说，该项目的失败是规划不善造成的。

ex.en: The committee agreed to investigate the full extent of the damage.
ex.zh: 委员会同意调查损失的全部范围。

ex.en: It is hard to measure the extent of public support for the reform.
ex.zh: 公众对这项改革的支持程度难以衡量。

senses: adj. 外部的,外面的,外表的
adj. 外部的，外在的；表面的
exterior.usage: adj.外部的，外面的 n.外观，外部；外貌

ex.en: The exterior of the house needs painting.
ex.zh: 房子外部需要粉刷。

ex.en: The hotel's plain exterior hides a luxuriously decorated interior.
ex.zh: 这家酒店朴实的外观背后是豪华的内部装修。

ex.en: Beneath his calm exterior, he was struggling with anxiety.
ex.zh: 在平静的外表之下，他内心饱受焦虑煎熬。

ex.en: The exterior walls were damaged by years of heavy rain.
ex.zh: 外墙因多年的大雨而受损。

senses: vt. 灭绝；根除；消灭；毁灭

ex.en: Farmers have long attempted to exterminate rats, yet the species continues to thrive alongside humans.
ex.zh: 农民长期以来一直试图消灭老鼠，但这一物种依然与人类相伴繁盛。

senses: adj. 外部的，外面的；外来的，外界的
external.usage: [反]internal a. 内部的；同义：outside, outer, exterior, surface；反义：internal adj. 内部的；adj.外部的；对外的；拓展：external challenge 外界的质疑；索引p408

ex.en: Many external influences can affect your state of mind.
ex.zh: 许多外在因素都可能影响人的心情。

ex.en: The committee will judge the design purely on its merits, ignoring all external pressure.
ex.zh: 委员会将完全根据设计本身的优点来评判，而不理会一切外部压力。

ex.en: external factors
ex.zh: 外部因素

senses: adj. 灭绝的，绝种的；不再存在的
extinct.usage: [族] extinction n. 灭绝；同义dead,gone;反义living adj.活的；索引p408

ex.en: When prehistoric man arrived in new parts of the world, something strange happened to the large animals: they suddenly became extinct.
ex.zh: 当史前人类到达世界的新区域时，某些奇怪的事情发生在大型动物身上：它们突然灭绝了。

ex.en: Scientists warn that hundreds of species may become extinct within this century.
ex.zh: 科学家警告说，数以百计的物种可能在本世纪内灭绝。

ex.en: Volcanoes in this region have long been extinct and covered with forest.
ex.zh: 该地区的火山早已熄灭，上面覆盖着森林。

extinction.usage: 词根记忆：ex(out，向外)+tinct(prick，刺)+ion(名词后缀)→向外拔刺→连根拔起→灭绝；索引p408

ex.en: "The federal government is giving responsibility for managing the bird to the same industries that are pushing it to extinction," says biologist Jay Lininger.
ex.zh: 生物学家杰·利宁格说：“联邦政府是在将管理该鸟类的责任推卸给那些将该鸟类推向灭绝的企业。”

ex.en: News of the bombing extinguished all hope of peace.
ex.zh: 轰炸的消息使和平的希望全部破灭。

ex.en: Firefighters took three hours to extinguish the warehouse fire.
ex.zh: 消防员花了三个小时才扑灭仓库大火。

ex.en: Nothing could extinguish her enthusiasm for medical research.
ex.zh: 什么都无法浇灭她对医学研究的热情。

ex.en: Smoking is prohibited, and all flames must be extinguished before leaving the site.
ex.zh: 禁止吸烟，离开现场前必须熄灭所有明火。

ex.en: Every laboratory must keep a fire extinguisher within easy reach and check it at regular intervals.
ex.zh: 每个实验室都必须在触手可及之处放置灭火器，并定期检查。

ex.en: Passengers pay an extra charge for luggage that exceeds the weight limit.
ex.zh: 乘客为超过重量限制的行李支付额外费用。

ex.en: She works extra hours at weekends to save for her master's degree.
ex.zh: 她周末加班攒钱攻读硕士学位。

ex.en: The hotel provides extra blankets during the cold winter months.
ex.zh: 酒店在寒冷的冬季提供额外的毯子。

senses: v. 抽出，拔出；提取；提炼
extract.usage: n.选段，引文；提取物 v.提取，提炼；摘录；ex（表示“往外”）+tract（拽，拉）→往外拽→抽出，拔出→提取，摘录。；词根:ex(out外)+tract(draw拉)→往外拉→提取；索引p408

ex.en: Corporate profits increasingly rely on extracting value from the public.
ex.zh: 企业的利润越来越依赖于从公众那里获取价值。

ex.en: So he hired a dentist to transplant nine teeth into his jaw—having extracted them from the mouths of his slaves.
ex.zh: 于是他聘请了一名牙医，在他的下颌里植入九颗牙，而这九颗牙都是从他家奴隶的嘴里拔出来的。

ex.en: The machine extracts salt from seawater at a surprisingly low cost.
ex.zh: 这种机器以低得惊人的成本从海水中提取盐分。

senses: n. [U,C] 提取；提炼；拔出；开采

ex.en: The extraction of oil from this region began more than a century ago.
ex.zh: 从该地区开采石油始于一个多世纪前。

ex.en: The extraction of the tooth took the dentist less than ten minutes.
ex.zh: 牙医拔那颗牙用了不到十分钟。

ex.en: She is of Irish extraction but grew up in Canada.
ex.zh: 她有爱尔兰血统，但在加拿大长大。

senses: a. 课外的；课程以外的
adj. 分外的;(尤指性关系)婚外的

ex.en: Participation in extracurricular activities helps students develop teamwork skills that classroom instruction alone cannot provide.
ex.zh: 参加课外活动有助于学生培养课堂单一教学无法提供的团队合作技能。

ex.en: The government refused to extradite the suspect, arguing that he would not receive a fair trial abroad.
ex.zh: 政府拒绝引渡这名嫌疑人，理由是他在国外不会受到公正审判。

senses: ad. 极其，极端地；非常奇怪地
adv. 非常,格外地,非凡地

ex.en: The museum's collection is extraordinarily rich in medieval manuscripts.
ex.zh: 该博物馆的中世纪手稿藏品异常丰富。

ex.en: He is an extraordinarily patient teacher who never loses his temper.
ex.zh: 他是一位极有耐心的老师，从不发脾气。

ex.en: Ordinary materials can be turned into extraordinarily beautiful works of art.
ex.zh: 普通材料也能被制成异常精美的艺术品。

senses: adj. 非常的,特别的,卓越的,意想不到的
adj. 非凡的，不平常的；令人惊奇的
extraordinary.usage: extra（超出）+ ordinary（普通的）→非凡的；adj.非凡的，卓越的；超出（extra）一般的（ordinary）→非凡的；索引p408

ex.en: She was a truly extraordinary woman.
ex.zh: 她是位非常杰出的女性。

ex.en: The athlete showed extraordinary courage in coming back after such a serious injury.
ex.zh: 这位运动员在如此严重的伤病后重返赛场，表现出非凡的勇气。

ex.en: It is extraordinary that the ancient bridge has survived so many earthquakes.
ex.zh: 令人惊奇的是，这座古桥经历了这么多次地震依然完好。

senses: n. 奢侈品；铺张浪费；奢华

ex.en: Such extravagance is shameful when there are people starving in the world.
ex.zh: 世界上还有人在挨饿，这样挥霍太可耻了。

senses: adj. 奢侈的，浪费的；过于昂贵的
extravagant.usage: excessive指数量范围过分到不合理;extravagant过度放肆奢侈,含愚蠢挥霍意;extreme极度极端,已达极点;反义thrifty节俭；extra（额外的）+vagant（发音类似“围巾”）→要买额外的围巾就是“奢侈的，浪费的”。；索引p408

ex.en: Fantasies of great wealth often involve visions of fancy cars and extravagant homes.
ex.zh: 对巨额财富的幻想往往包括对豪华汽车和豪华住宅的幻想。

ex.en: Critics condemned the council's extravagant spending on its new headquarters.
ex.zh: 批评者谴责议会在新总部上的奢靡开支。

ex.en: It would be extravagant to buy a new laptop when this one still works.
ex.zh: 这台笔记本电脑还能用，再买新的就太浪费了。

ex.en: His extravagant claims about the product were not supported by any evidence.
ex.zh: 他对该产品的夸大宣传毫无证据支持。

senses: adv. 挥霍地；无节制地；过分地

ex.en: The festival had become so extravagantly expensive that many local families could no longer afford to take part.
ex.zh: 这个节庆变得奢华昂贵，许多当地家庭已负担不起参加的费用。

senses: n. 极端；完全相反的事物

ex.en: In physics, one approach takes this impulse for unification to its extreme, and seeks a theory of everything—a single generative equation for all we see.
ex.zh: 在物理学上，有一种方法将这种追求统一性的冲动发挥到极致，并试图找到一个万能的理论，即一个能解释我们所见的一切的通用公式。

ex.en: Athletes who train in extreme heat risk serious dehydration.
ex.zh: 在酷热中训练的运动员有严重脱水的风险。

ex.en: His political views lie at the extreme right of the spectrum.
ex.zh: 他的政治观点属于极右翼。

ex.en: She went to extreme lengths to keep her private life secret.
ex.zh: 她竭尽全力对自己的私生活保密。

ex.en: The manuscript was extremely rare, and only two copies are known to have survived.
ex.zh: 这份手稿极其罕见，据悉仅有两份存世。

senses: adj. 外在的，外来的；非固有的；非本质的

ex.en: Nowadays there are fewer extrinsic pressures to get married.
ex.zh: 现在，结婚与否很少受到来自外部的压力。

ex.en: She was motivated by the idea of extrinsic rewards such as salary rather than intrinsic ones such as pride and self-respect.
ex.zh: 她受到外在奖励（如薪水）而不是内在奖励（如骄傲和自尊）的激励。

senses: n. 眼睛；针眼；眼光；视力
eye.usage: keep an eye on...照看；留意

ex.en: The report keeps a close eye on how climate change affects coastal cities across Europe.
ex.zh: 该报告密切关注气候变化如何影响欧洲沿海城市。

eyebrow.usage: [记] eye（眼睛）+brow（额头）→眼睛上方额头下方的毛发→眉毛

ex.en: The minister's controversial remarks raised eyebrows among economists who had expected a cautious budget.
ex.zh: 这位部长有争议的言论令原本预期预算会趋于谨慎的经济学家们感到惊讶。

ex.en: Hours of screen time every day can gradually damage children's eyesight.
ex.zh: 每天长时间盯着屏幕会逐渐损害儿童视力。

ex.en: His eyesight has deteriorated so much that he can no longer read without glasses.
ex.zh: 他的视力衰退严重，不戴眼镜已无法阅读。

ex.en: Regular eye tests help detect problems with eyesight at an early stage.
ex.zh: 定期眼科检查有助于尽早发现视力问题。

ex.en: Water freezes at 32 degrees on the Fahrenheit scale, though most scientists now prefer Celsius measurements.
ex.zh: 水在华氏温标 32 度时结冰，不过如今多数科学家更倾向于使用摄氏计量。

fable.usage: 助记:able(有能力的)作家喜欢创作fable(寓言)

ex.en: In the ancient fable, a slow but determined tortoise defeats a boastful hare in a race.
ex.zh: 在这则古老的寓言中，一只缓慢而坚定的乌龟在赛跑中击败了自夸的野兔。

ex.en: Cheap imported fabric dominated the market, forcing local mills to cut costs or close entirely.
ex.zh: 廉价的进口布料占据了市场，迫使当地纺织厂削减成本或彻底关闭。

senses: vt. 捏造,编造(谎言,借口等)
fabricate.usage: 同义:construct,invent;反义:destroy;派生:fabrication n.制造;虚构物；工厂（factory）不制造（fabricate）这种布料（fabric）的衣服。

ex.en: These specialized chips will be fabricated by Microsoft.
ex.zh: 这些专用芯片将由微软公司制造。

senses: n. 虚构的信息，捏造的故事

ex.en: Her story was a complete fabrication from start to finish.
ex.zh: 她的叙述从头至尾都是编造出来的。

senses: a. 极好的；绝妙的；巨大的；神话寓言中的
fabulous.usage: 派生fabulously adv.难以置信地；fabu（发布）+l（了）+ous（后缀）→书发布了，对我是“极好的”。；索引p408

ex.en: They put on a fabulous performance.
ex.zh: 他们上演了一场精彩的表演。

ex.en: The startup earned a fabulous sum within a single year of trading.
ex.zh: 这家初创公司在开业一年之内就赚得了一笔巨款。

ex.en: We had a fabulous time exploring the old town on foot.
ex.zh: 我们徒步游览老城，玩得开心极了。

face.usage: confront 的近义词；be faced with...面临……；face up to 大胆面对;to one's face 当面,公开

ex.en: Manufacturers face rising pressure to reduce emissions while keeping their products affordable for ordinary consumers.
ex.zh: 制造商面临在保持产品价格亲民的同时减少排放的日益增大的压力。

ex.en: The book examines every facet of urban life, from transport and housing to leisure and crime.
ex.zh: 本书审视城市生活的方方面面，从交通、住房到休闲和犯罪。

ex.en: Researchers found that even brief facial expressions can influence how strangers judge our trustworthiness.
ex.zh: 研究人员发现，即使是短暂的面部表情也会影响陌生人对我们可信度的判断。

senses: vt. 使变得(更)容易,使便利
facilitate.usage: 比 promote 更侧重提供便利条件使事情容易；fac（做）+ilit+ate→使好做→促进。近义：promote vt. 促进；派生facilitation n.便利；索引p408

ex.en: The new software is designed to facilitate communication between departments.
ex.zh: 新软件旨在促进部门之间的沟通。

ex.en: Good transport links facilitate the movement of goods and people.
ex.zh: 便利的交通促进货物和人员的流动。

ex.en: Teachers should facilitate discussion rather than simply lecture students.
ex.zh: 教师应当引导讨论，而不只是向学生灌输。

facility.usage: infrastructure 的近义词；常用复数facilities；fac(make做)+ility(名词后缀)→经常去做→熟练；fac（做）+il（易于，善于）+ity（名词后缀）→易于做事→带来便利之物→设备，设施；拓展：local facilities 当地的设施；索引p408

ex.en: The hotel provides excellent facilities for children.
ex.zh: 这家旅馆的儿童设施十分完善。

ex.en: The new research facility will open to scientists from other universities.
ex.zh: 新的研究设施将向其他大学的科学家开放。

ex.en: He has a remarkable facility for learning foreign languages.
ex.zh: 他在学习外语方面有非凡的天赋。

phrases.m: （用于探讨真实事情的意义）…这一事实

ex.en: Some might see the proposal as a booby prize for the fact that Britain is no longer able to apply for the much more prestigious title of European capital of culture.
ex.zh: 一些人或许会认为这个提议只是个安慰奖，因为事实是英国不再有实力再次申请欧洲文化之都这一更负盛名的称号。

ex.en: The article ignores the fact that most customers prefer lower prices to faster delivery.
ex.zh: 这篇文章忽视了一个事实：大多数顾客宁愿价格更低也不在乎送货更快。

ex.en: Scientists must separate fact from opinion when reporting their findings.
ex.zh: 科学家在报告研究结果时必须把事实与观点分开。

ex.en: Owing to the fact that demand keeps rising, prices are unlikely to fall.
ex.zh: 由于需求持续上升，价格不太可能下降。

senses: n. [C] 仿真陈述；花絮新闻，趣闻
n. 令人信以为真的报导;有趣消息;趣闻

ex.en: The article opens with a factoid about coffee consumption designed to grab the reader's attention.
ex.zh: 这篇文章以一条关于咖啡消费量的趣闻开头，旨在吸引读者的注意力。

factor.usage: fact(做)+-or(物)→起作用之物→因素；[近] element；[构]fact（事实）+ or→因素；n.因素，要素；等级，系数；因 子 v.把……作为因素计入做代理商；词根记忆：fact(make,制作)+or→制作出的东西→组成部分→因素；索引p408

ex.en: Another factor may be that more people are trying to overpack their carry-on bags to avoid checked-baggage fees, though the airlines strongly dispute this.
ex.zh: 另一因素可能是越来越多的乘客为了避免支付托运行李费用,过度打包随身携带行李,而航空公司极力反对这一点。

ex.en: Cost is not the only factor in customers' buying decisions.
ex.zh: 成本并非顾客购买决策的唯一因素。

ex.en: Safety was a key factor in the design of the new bridge.
ex.zh: 安全是设计这座新桥时的一个关键因素。

ex.en: The car factory employs more than three thousand local workers.
ex.zh: 这家汽车工厂雇用了三千多名当地工人。

ex.en: Factory output rose slightly last quarter after months of decline.
ex.zh: 经过数月下滑后，工厂产量上季度略有回升。

ex.en: New regulations require factories to cut their emissions by half.
ex.zh: 新法规要求工厂将排放量减半。

factual.usage: 联想记忆：和fact(n.事实)一起记；索引p408

ex.en: A good book review should distinguish clearly between factual claims and the author's personal opinions.
ex.zh: 一篇好的书评应清楚区分事实性陈述和作者的个人观点。

senses: n. (学院或系的)全体教学人员(u)
n. 全体教师；系；院；才能，能力
n. （高等院校的）院系；（高等院校中院、系的）全体教员；能力

ex.en: In the 1960s and 1970s, European universities saw marked changes in their governance arrangements, with empowerment of junior faculty and to some degree of students as well.
ex.zh: 在20世纪60年代和70年代，欧洲大学的管理安排发生了显著变化，赋予了初级教师权力，在某种程度上也赋予了学生权力。

ex.en: When a faculty or department grows from, say, five to 20 members within three or four years, and when the new staff are predominantly young men and women fresh from postgraduate study, they largely define the norms of academic life in that faculty.
ex.zh: 比如说，当某一院系在三四年内就从五名成员增加到20名成员，并且当新员工主要是刚刚毕业的研究生时，他们就在很大程度上确定了该院系学术生活的规范。

ex.en: The university plans to hire twenty new faculty members next year.
ex.zh: 该大学计划明年聘请二十名新教师。

ex.en: Even in old age she retained her mental faculties.
ex.zh: 即使到了晚年，她的心智能力依然完好。

senses: n. 一时的风尚,短暂的狂热

ex.en: Diets based on a single food are usually a passing fad rather than sound nutritional advice.
ex.zh: 只吃单一食物的饮食法通常只是一时的风尚，而非可靠的营养建议。

senses: vt. (声音等)变微弱;(光等)变暗淡
fade.usage: fade away逐渐消失；同义:discolour;dim,pale;disappear,vanish；发音类似"废的"：羊毛衫洗一次就废了褪色了；② vi. 逐渐变弱（2017年翻译）；索引p408

ex.en: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older.
ex.zh: 其他研究表明，叛逆行为随着你进入青少年时期而增加，然后随着年龄的增长而消失。

ex.en: But even as the number of English speakers expands further there are signs that the global predominance of the language may fade within the foreseeable future.
ex.zh: 但是，尽管说英语的人在不断增多，却仍有迹象表明：在可预见的未来，英语的全球主导地位可能会逐渐减弱。

ex.en: The photographs had faded badly after years in the sunlight.
ex.zh: 在阳光照射多年之后，这些照片已经严重褪色。

fail.usage: fail to do sth.未能做某事；反义:pass 及格;if all else fails 实在不行的话；索引p408

ex.en: The company failed to deliver the goods on time.
ex.zh: 该公司未能按时交货。

ex.en: Thousands of students fail their driving test each year.
ex.zh: 每年有数千名学生没有通过驾照考试。

ex.en: When the power supply failed, the whole hospital switched to backup generators.
ex.zh: 电力供应中断时，整座医院改用备用发电机。

ex.en: The report identifies poor time management as the most common failing among first-year undergraduates.
ex.zh: 报告指出，时间管理能力差是大学一年级新生最常见的缺点。

failure.usage: [反]success n. 成功；power failure 断电;heart failure 心力衰竭；索引p408

ex.en: The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure.
ex.zh: C级和A级管理者之间的区别很可能决定了一个企业成功与否。

ex.en: The failure of the peace talks disappointed the international community.
ex.zh: 和谈失败令国际社会失望。

ex.en: A failure in the cooling system forced the reactor to shut down.
ex.zh: 冷却系统故障迫使反应堆关闭。

ex.en: He regarded his first business failure as a valuable lesson.
ex.zh: 他把第一次生意失败当作宝贵的教训。

senses: adj. 不清楚的,模糊的,微弱的
adj. （光、声、味）微弱的；不清楚的；可能性不大的；昏厥的
faint.usage: [近]weak a. 微弱的；哪怕可能性不大（faint），你也要有信心（faith）。；索引p408

ex.en: The heat made him feel faint.
ex.zh: 炎热使他觉得快要晕倒了。

ex.en: A faint smell of paint lingered in the newly decorated office.
ex.zh: 新装修的办公室里残留着一股淡淡的油漆味。

ex.en: There is a faint chance that the lost manuscript will still turn up.
ex.zh: 那份遗失的手稿仍有渺茫的机会重现于世。

fair.usage: 近just；反unfair；[反]unfair a. 不公平的；fair play 公平合理;反义:unfair 不公正的；adj.公平的；相当大的；浅色 的；晴朗的；美丽的 adv.公平地，公正地；非常；索引p408

ex.en: To be fair, the FSA says it is not telling people to cut out roast foods entirely, but to reduce their lifetime intake.
ex.zh: 公平地说，食品标准局(FSA)并不是建议人们完全戒除烤制食物，而是减少他们一生的摄入量。

ex.en: It is not fair to judge a student by a single examination.
ex.zh: 仅凭一次考试来评判学生是不公平的。

ex.en: The book fair attracts publishers from all over the world every spring.
ex.zh: 每年春天，这个书博会吸引世界各地的出版商前来。

fairly.usage: [辨]fairly相当（程度适中）；辨析程度副词语气由弱到强:fairly<quite<rather<pretty；adv.相当地；公正地；简直；索引p408

ex.en: The test is fairly difficult, but most students managed to pass.
ex.zh: 这个测试相当难，但大多数学生还是设法通过了。

ex.en: The profits were shared fairly among all the partners.
ex.zh: 利润在所有合伙人之间公平分配。

ex.en: She felt fairly confident about the interview despite her limited experience.
ex.zh: 尽管经验有限，她对这次面试还是颇有信心。

ex.en: Voters expect fairness in the way electoral districts are drawn.
ex.zh: 选民期望选区划分做到公平。

ex.en: The teacher's fairness earned her the respect of all the students.
ex.zh: 这位老师办事公正，赢得了全体学生的尊重。

ex.en: Rules on fairness in hiring help to reduce discrimination at work.
ex.zh: 招聘公平方面的规定有助于减少职场歧视。

ex.en: In the old fairy tale, a poor woodcutter is rewarded for his kindness by a mysterious stranger.
ex.zh: 在这个古老的童话里，一位贫苦的樵夫因善良而得到神秘陌生人的奖赏。

senses: n. 信任；相信；宗教信仰；宗教
faith.usage: have faith in...对……有信心；in bad faith存心欺诈地；n.信心，信念；宗教信仰；忠 诚；串词记忆：考试不及格(fail)，信心(faith)大减；索引p408

ex.en: On the other hand, putting your faith in the wrong place often carries a high price.
ex.zh: 另一方面，在错误的地方施以信任往往会付出高昂的代价。

ex.en: Despite repeated failures, she never lost faith in her own ability.
ex.zh: 尽管屡遭失败，她从未对自己的能力失去信心。

ex.en: The report shook public faith in the safety of the new drug.
ex.zh: 该报告动摇了公众对这种新药安全性的信心。

faithful.usage: faith(忠诚)+ful→忠诚的;辨析:faithful因允诺、誓言而忠于某人;loyal愿不惜牺牲、不怕艰难而效忠

ex.en: The biography remains faithful to the facts, drawing heavily on letters the scientist wrote to colleagues.
ex.zh: 这部传记忠于事实，大量引用了这位科学家写给同事的信件。

faithfulness.usage: 联想：faith(信任)+ful形容词后缀+ness名词后缀→忠诚；索引p408

ex.en: The translator's faithfulness to the original text sometimes came at the cost of elegance in English.
ex.zh: 译者对原文的忠诚有时以牺牲英文的优雅为代价。

senses: n. 赝品,假消息,假动作；骗子,冒充者
v. 伪造(某物)；假装,佯装
fake.usage: 派生faker n.伪造者,骗子,冒牌货；adj.伪造的，冒充的；虚假的 n.假货，贋品；冒充者 v.伪造，冒充；假装；索引p408

ex.en: Undercover investigators were able to sneak weapons—both fake and real—past airport security nearly every time they tried.
ex.zh: 卧底调查员能够偷偷携带武器（不管真假）成功通过机场安检，几乎屡试不爽。

ex.en: Experts warn that consumers can hardly tell fake luxury bags from genuine ones.
ex.zh: 专家警告说，消费者几乎无法分辨假冒名牌包与真品。

ex.en: He faked illness to avoid attending the compulsory training session.
ex.zh: 他假装生病，以逃避参加那次强制性培训。

senses: vi. 落下；跌倒；（数量）减少
fall.usage: fall behind落后；fall back on 求助于;fall in with 符合,一致;fall out 争吵,结果是；词组还有 fall sick/ill 生病，得病；索引p408

ex.en: Worse, the numbers are now falling at an accelerating rate.
ex.zh: 更糟糕的是，数量（指成年人每周锻炼的人数）目前正在急剧下降。

ex.en: Prices fell sharply after the government lifted import restrictions.
ex.zh: 政府取消进口限制后，价格大幅下跌。

ex.en: In fall, the national park attracts crowds of photographers.
ex.zh: 秋天，这个国家公园吸引了大批摄影师。

senses: n. [U] 放射性沉降物；后果；余波
fallout.usage: n.放射性坠尘；后果，余波；易混辨析：指某种情况或者行动带来的不良后果或者产生的余波；索引p408

ex.en: The fallout from the scandal damaged the reputation of the entire department.
ex.zh: 丑闻的余波损害了整个部门的声誉。

ex.en: The financial crisis produced political fallout that lasted for a decade.
ex.zh: 金融危机造成的政治后遗症持续了十年。

ex.en: Officials warned of radioactive fallout after the accident at the plant.
ex.zh: 电厂事故发生后，官员们就放射性沉降物发出警告。

senses: adj. 谬误的,虚伪的,假的

ex.en: Social media platforms struggle to stop the spread of false information during election campaigns.
ex.zh: 社交媒体平台难以阻止虚假信息在竞选期间传播。

senses: n. 虚假,说谎,不实之词,谎言

ex.en: The article repeated several falsehoods about the safety of the vaccine.
ex.zh: 这篇文章重复了有关疫苗安全性的若干不实之词。

ex.en: He never deliberately told a falsehood in all his years as a witness.
ex.zh: 他做证人的那些年里从未故意说过谎。

ex.en: Internet companies are under pressure to remove falsehoods from their platforms.
ex.zh: 互联网公司面临压力，须从平台上清除虚假信息。

ex.en: In 'fame' and 'famous', the root 'fam-' carries the sense of reputation or being widely known.
ex.zh: 在 fame 和 famous 中，词根 fam- 含有名声或广为人知之意。

fame.usage: [族]famous a. 著名的；fam（名声）+e→名声；a striving for fame 追求名誉；n.名誉，名气；索引p408

ex.en: Part of the fame of Allen's book is its contention that "Circumstances do not make a person, they reveal him."
ex.zh: 艾伦的著作享有盛誉，部分原因是他提出的"环境不能塑造人，环境只是彰显人"的主张。

ex.en: The young scientist won international fame for her work on vaccines.
ex.zh: 这位年轻科学家因其在疫苗方面的研究而赢得国际声誉。

ex.en: He cared little for fame and refused most interview requests.
ex.zh: 他淡泊名声，拒绝了大多数采访请求。

ex.en: The city, famed for its universities, attracts students from every corner of the world.
ex.zh: 这座以大学闻名的城市吸引着来自世界各地的学生。

senses: adj. 亲近的,过分冒昧的,随便的
familiar.usage: be familiar with（人）熟悉；be familiar to为……所熟知；派生familiarity n.熟悉,通晓；随和,亲近

ex.en: Doctors are familiar with the symptoms of the disease, yet early diagnosis remains surprisingly rare.
ex.zh: 医生们熟悉这种疾病的症状，但早期诊断仍然出奇地少见。

senses: n. 家庭；孩子；科；语族，语系；家族
n. 家,家庭成员(常用复数)
family.usage: 作“家人”讲时谓语动词可用复数；辨析:family指组成家庭的成员;home家,带感情色彩;house房屋,单指建筑物

ex.en: Balancing a demanding career with family responsibilities is a challenge many working parents know well.
ex.zh: 在高强度的工作与家庭责任之间取得平衡，是许多职场父母深有体会的难题。

famine.usage: 没有农民伯伯farmer的辛勤，很多人面临饥荒famine

ex.en: When famine strikes, it is often women and children who suffer the most.
ex.zh: 发生饥荒时，受害最深的往往是妇女和儿童。

ex.en: Drought and war combined to create famine conditions across the region.
ex.zh: 干旱与战争叠加，使整个地区陷入饥荒。

ex.en: International aid was rushed to the famine zone within days.
ex.zh: 国际援助几天内就紧急送到了饥荒地区。

ex.en: Historians blame the famine on failed harvests and poor government planning.
ex.zh: 历史学家将这场饥荒归咎于歉收和政府规划不力。

ex.en: The university is famous for its research on renewable energy rather than its long history.
ex.zh: 这所大学以其可再生能源研究而非悠久历史而闻名。

senses: n. 扇子,风扇;(影,球等)迷

ex.en: The novelist has a loyal fan base that follows her work across genres and languages.
ex.zh: 这位小说家拥有忠实的粉丝群，追随她跨越题材和语言的作品。

senses: adj. [usually before noun] 昂贵的；精致的花哨的；奢华的
fancy.usage: fancy doing sth.想要做某事；作形容词；辨析:fancy常指不切实际的想象;imagination指合乎情理而富创造性的想象；发音类似烦死→备考特别烦的时候，不如坐那儿想象一下自己考上以后的美好时光，瞬间就有了斗志→想象

ex.en: Most designers with a top fashion house will stay on for several years, working on fancy clothes.
ex.zh: 顶级时装公司的设计师大多会留任多年，设计精致服装。

ex.en: She fancied (that) she could hear footsteps.
ex.zh: 她觉得好像听到了脚步声。

ex.en: They stayed at a fancy hotel overlooking the harbour.
ex.zh: 他们住在一家可以俯瞰海港的豪华酒店。

ex.en: She took a fancy to the old house the moment she saw it.
ex.zh: 她第一眼看到那座老房子就喜欢上了。

ex.en: Children often fantasise about becoming famous, yet few appreciate the pressures that fame brings.
ex.zh: 孩子们常常幻想成名，却很少有人体会到名望带来的压力。

ex.en: Some critics argue that tourists fantasise about exotic destinations rather than engaging with real local cultures.
ex.zh: 一些批评者认为，游客幻想充满异域风情的目的地，却不去接触真实的当地文化。

senses: adj. 奇异的,异想天开的；极好的
adj. 怪诞的；极好的；不切实际的
adj. 极好的；大得难以置信的；怪诞的；不切实际的
fantastic.usage: 亦拼作fantastical;派生fantastically adv.异乎寻常地；真 fantastic ideas 极妙的主意

ex.en: This was a fantastic opportunity for students.
ex.zh: 这对学生来说是一个极好的机会。

ex.en: The volunteers did a fantastic job of cleaning up the beach.
ex.zh: 志愿者们清理海滩的工作做得非常出色。

ex.en: The novel describes a fantastic world where animals can speak.
ex.zh: 这部小说描写了一个动物会说话的奇幻世界。

ex.en: The scheme paid fantastic sums of money for very little work.
ex.zh: 该计划为极少的工作支付了高得惊人的报酬。

ex.en: The paintings depict fantastical creatures that seem to have escaped from an illustrated storybook.
ex.zh: 这些画描绘了奇幻的生物，仿佛是从绘本故事书中逃出来的。

fantasy.usage: 发音类似范特思→范特思是一个爱做白日梦的人→幻想，想象；索引p408

ex.en: On display here are various fantasy elements whose reference, at some basic level, seems to be the natural world.
ex.zh: 此处展示的是各种幻想元素，在某些基本层面上，这些元素的参照物就是自然世界。

ex.en: He lives in a fantasy world where nothing ever goes wrong.
ex.zh: 他生活在一个万事顺遂的幻想世界里。

ex.en: Winning the lottery is a common fantasy among people trapped in dull jobs.
ex.zh: 中彩票是困于乏味工作的人们常有的幻想。

ex.en: The film blends historical fact with fantasy in a striking way.
ex.zh: 影片将史实与幻想以惊人的方式融合在一起。

ex.en: So far, attempts to restore the wetlands have met with only limited success.
ex.zh: 迄今为止，恢复湿地的尝试仅取得了有限的成功。

senses: adj. 荒唐的;荒谬的;可笑的

ex.en: He described the licensing procedure as farcical, noting that applications took months to be processed.
ex.zh: 他形容许可证审批程序荒唐可笑，指出申请要数月才能得到处理。

senses: vi. [not usually in progressive tenses] 进展
n. 车费,船费,飞机票价;伙食,饮食
fare.usage: [近]fee n. 费用；辨析:fare车船费;fee酬金/手续费/学费;pay工资薪金;wage工人工资常用复数；去很远的(far)地方需要“车费(fare)”

ex.en: But the researchers think they have come up with a plan to keep their underground ticket fares low.
ex.zh: 但研究人员认为他们已经想出了一个把地铁票价维持在低位的方案。

ex.en: Bus fares will rise by ten per cent from next month.
ex.zh: 公交车票价将从下个月起上涨百分之十。

ex.en: How did you fare in your final examinations?
ex.zh: 你期末考试考得怎么样？

ex.en: Critics complained that standard rail fares were far too high.
ex.zh: 批评者抱怨普通火车票价太高。

farewell.usage: fare+well→一路平安→告别；fare(车费)+well(好)→付好车费后跟司机说“再会”→告别

ex.en: Colleagues gathered to say farewell to the retiring professor.
ex.zh: 同事们聚在一起向退休的教授告别。

ex.en: The band announced its farewell tour after twenty years together.
ex.zh: 乐队宣布将在成军二十年后举行告别巡演。

ex.en: He gave a moving farewell speech at his last board meeting.
ex.zh: 他在最后一次董事会上发表了感人的告别演说。

senses: vt.&vi. 务农；种田；从事畜牧业

ex.en: The family farm survived the recession by selling produce directly to customers at weekend markets.
ex.zh: 这家家庭农场靠周末集市上直接向顾客出售农产品熬过了经济衰退。

ex.en: Each farmer interviewed for the study reported lower yields after the drought of last summer.
ex.zh: 这项研究采访的每位农民都报告说，去年夏天的干旱之后收成有所下降。

ex.en: Traditional farming methods, though slower, cause far less damage to the soil than intensive agriculture.
ex.zh: 传统耕作方式虽然较慢，但对土壤的破坏远小于集约化农业。

ex.en: The council's farsighted decision to protect the wetlands preserved a habitat that developers had coveted for years.
ex.zh: 市政会保护湿地的远见之举，保住了开发商觊觎多年的栖息地。

ex.en: The new railway station lies farther from the city centre than commuters had been promised.
ex.zh: 新火车站距离市中心的距离比通勤者原先被承诺的更远。

senses: v. 强烈地吸引,迷住,使神魂颠倒
fascinate.usage: [族]fascinating a. 迷人的；辨析近义:interest感兴趣;excite兴奋;attract吸引;fascinate迷住程度更深;反义:bore

ex.en: Documentaries about deep-sea creatures continue to fascinate audiences who will never see them in person.
ex.zh: 关于深海生物的纪录片持续吸引着那些永远不会亲眼见到它们的观众。

senses: adj. 极有吸引力的；迷人的

ex.en: And it transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.
ex.zh: 同时，公共历史也因此发生了转变：下层人民的生活和上流社会的一样丰富多彩。

ex.en: His lifelong fascination with the stars began when his father gave him a second-hand telescope.
ex.zh: 他对星空的毕生迷恋始于父亲送给他一台二手望远镜之时。

ex.en: Historians continue to debate why fascism appealed to so many Europeans during the economic crisis of the 1930s.
ex.zh: 历史学家仍在争论，为什么法西斯主义在二十世纪三十年代经济危机期间吸引了这么多欧洲人。

senses: n. 时兴式样；流行款式；时尚；时装业

ex.en: The fashion industry knows it has an inherent problem in focusing on material adornment and idealized body types.
ex.zh: 时尚界清楚自己在注重物质装饰和理想化身材方面存在固有问题。

ex.en: Loose clothing came back into fashion after a decade of slim fits.
ex.zh: 宽松服装在修身款式流行十年后重新时尚起来。

ex.en: The bridge was built in the fashion of the nineteenth century.
ex.zh: 这座桥是仿照十九世纪的样式建造的。

ex.en: Each family celebrates the festival in its own fashion.
ex.zh: 每个家庭都以自己的方式庆祝这个节日。

ex.en: It's becoming fashionable to have long hair again.
ex.zh: 现在又开始流行留长发了。

ex.en: Newly fashionable health-savings plans are spreading from legislative halls to Wal-Mart workers.
ex.zh: 新近流行的健康储蓄计划正从议会大厅蔓延到沃尔玛员工那里。

ex.en: Cycling to work has become fashionable among young office workers.
ex.zh: 骑自行车上班在年轻上班族中已成时尚。

senses: a. 迅速的；立即发生的；头脑灵活的
adj. 快的,迅速的;紧的,牢的
adv. 快地,迅速地;紧紧地,牢固地

ex.en: Cities are changing fast, and planners must anticipate needs that residents have not yet voiced.
ex.zh: 城市变化迅速，规划者必须预见到居民尚未表达出来的需求。

ex.en: Critics blame fast-food advertising for children's poor eating habits and rising obesity rates.
ex.zh: 批评者将儿童不良饮食习惯和不断上升的肥胖率归咎于快餐广告。

senses: v. [usually passive] 系紧；扣上；把…固定
v. 扎牢,使固定,使牢固
fasten.usage: fast+（e）n→系紧；fast(牢固的)+en(动词后缀,使……)→使牢固

ex.en: Please fasten your seat belts.
ex.zh: 请系好安全带。

ex.en: Fasten the strap tightly so that the box will not slide about.
ex.zh: 把带子系紧，这样箱子就不会滑动。

ex.en: Passengers were asked to fasten their seat belts before landing.
ex.zh: 乘客被要求在着陆前系好安全带。

ex.en: She fastened the notice to the board with four pins.
ex.zh: 她用四枚图钉把通知固定在告示板上。

senses: a. 肥胖的；厚的；宽大的；大量的；值钱的

ex.en: Nutrition labels list the amount of fat in each serving so consumers can compare products.
ex.zh: 营养成分标签列出了每份食品的脂肪含量，以便消费者比较不同产品。

senses: 宿命的,命运的,命中注定的
fatal.usage: 派生fatally adv. 致命地,注定地；发音类似"肥头"→婴儿得了大头病是很致命的；索引p408

ex.en: Since the beginning, this price tag has been PreCheck's fatal flaw.
ex.zh: 从一开始，这个价格标签就是预检的致命缺陷。

ex.en: The driver suffered fatal injuries when his car crashed into a tree.
ex.zh: 司机的汽车撞到树上，他受了致命伤。

ex.en: A small error in the code proved fatal to the whole space mission.
ex.zh: 代码中的一个小错误对整个航天任务来说是致命的。

senses: n. 命运；命中注定的事

ex.en: The fate of the rainforest may be decided within the next decade.
ex.zh: 雨林的命运可能在未来十年内决定。

ex.en: Many islanders fear that rising seas will seal the fate of their homes.
ex.zh: 许多岛民担心，海平面上升将注定他们家园的命运。

ex.en: She accepted her fate calmly and began planning a new career.
ex.zh: 她平静地接受了自己的命运，开始规划新的职业。

ex.en: His father worked in a shipyard, an experience that shaped the boy's views on labour.
ex.zh: 他的父亲在造船厂工作，这段经历塑造了这个男孩对劳动的看法。

fatigue.usage: fat(胖的)+i(我)+gue(谐音“哥”)→我哥有点胖，稍微一活动就感觉很“疲劳”；索引p408

ex.en: However, even though it's common, it's vital to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may regret for a long time.
ex.zh: 然而，即便这种情况很常见，你也需要记住一件事：在你疲惫不堪的一瞬间，你可能会对孩子说出一些自己可能会后悔很久的话。

ex.en: Driver fatigue is a major cause of motorway accidents.
ex.zh: 疲劳驾驶是高速公路事故的主要原因。

ex.en: Physical fatigue can weaken the immune system over time.
ex.zh: 身体疲劳久而久之会削弱免疫系统。

ex.en: The nurses worked twelve-hour shifts and suffered from constant fatigue.
ex.zh: 护士们轮班工作十二小时，一直疲惫不堪。

fault.usage: find fault with...挑剔……；发音类似“for（为）了（l）他（t）”→为了他，我曾经犯了很多“错误”

ex.en: The accident was not the driver's fault; the road was covered with ice.
ex.zh: 事故不是司机的过错，是路面结了冰。

ex.en: There is a small fault in the engine that causes the noise.
ex.zh: 发动机有个小故障，产生了这种噪音。

ex.en: Her only fault is that she is often late for meetings.
ex.zh: 她唯一的缺点是开会经常迟到。

senses: adj. 有缺点的,有错误的
adj. 有错误的，有缺陷的
adj. (思维方法)错误的；有缺陷的
faulty.usage: fault(过错)+y(形容词后缀)→有错误的；索引p408

ex.en: The fire was traced to a faulty wire in the attic.
ex.zh: 火灾起因被查明是阁楼里一根有故障的电线。

ex.en: The study was criticised for relying on faulty data.
ex.zh: 该研究因依赖有缺陷的数据而受到批评。

ex.en: Customers may return faulty goods for a full refund within thirty days.
ex.zh: 顾客可在三十天内退回有缺陷的商品并获得全额退款。

senses: n. [U,C] （某地区或某时期的）动物群

ex.en: The island's unique fauna evolved in isolation for millions of years before humans first arrived.
ex.zh: 该岛独特的动物群在与世隔绝的状态中演化了数百万年，直到人类首次到来。

ex.en: Critics argue that the tax cut will favor large corporations over small family businesses.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，减税将有利于大公司而不利于小型家族企业。

ex.en: Reviewers responded favorably to the biography, praising its careful research and lively style.
ex.zh: 书评人对这部传记反应良好，称赞其研究严谨、文笔生动。

favorite.usage: adj.最受喜爱的 n.受喜爱的人(或事物)

ex.en: The park quickly became a favorite picnic spot for families living in the crowded northern districts.
ex.zh: 这座公园很快成为居住在拥挤北部城区的家庭最喜爱的野餐地点。

ex.en: Employees accused the manager of favoritism after several relatives were promoted without open competition.
ex.zh: 在几名亲属未经公开竞争便获得晋升后，员工们指责经理偏袒徇私。

favour.usage: in favour of支持；赞成；亦作 favor；索引p408

ex.en: But a number of anthropologists in the early 1900s also rejected the particularist theory of culture in favor of diffusionism.
ex.zh: 但是20世纪早期的许多人类学家也支持文化传播论而反对文化特殊论。

ex.en: Could you do me a favour and post this letter?
ex.zh: 你能帮我个忙把这封信寄了吗？

ex.en: Recent surveys show that most voters favour higher taxes on tobacco.
ex.zh: 最新调查显示，大多数选民赞成提高烟草税。

ex.en: The court ruled in favour of the employees who had been unfairly dismissed.
ex.zh: 法院判那些被不公平解雇的员工胜诉。

ex.en: For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least.
ex.zh: 至少可以说，大部分人的反应都是赞同的。

ex.en: The film received favourable reviews from nearly every major critic.
ex.zh: 这部电影几乎得到了所有主要影评人的好评。

ex.en: The treaty created favourable conditions for foreign investment.
ex.zh: 该条约为外国投资创造了有利条件。

ex.en: The team is in a favourable position after winning its first two matches.
ex.zh: 该队在前两场比赛获胜后占据了有利位置。

ex.en: Early trials suggest patients respond favourably to the new drug, though larger studies are needed.
ex.zh: 早期试验表明患者对新药反应良好，不过仍需要更大规模的研究。

senses: n. 特别喜爱的人（或事物）

ex.en: The café quickly became a favourite meeting place for students preparing for their final exams.
ex.zh: 这家咖啡馆很快成为备考期末考试的学生们喜爱的聚会场所。

ex.en: The selection process was redesigned to eliminate favouritism and ensure that all candidates received equal treatment.
ex.zh: 选拔程序经过重新设计，以杜绝偏袒，确保所有候选人得到平等对待。

ex.en: Although email has largely replaced it, the fax machine is still used by some hospitals and law firms.
ex.zh: 尽管电子邮件已基本取代传真，一些医院和律师事务所仍在使用传真机。

fear.usage: for fear of doing sth.以免做某事

ex.en: Employees fear that automation will eliminate jobs faster than the economy can create new ones.
ex.zh: 员工们担心自动化消除工作岗位的速度会快于经济创造新岗位的速度。

senses: a. 恐惧的；害怕的；严重的；极坏的
fearful.usage: 发音类似"飞蛾忽"→飞蛾忽然飞过来吓我一大跳→可怕的；索引p408

ex.en: Parents are ever fearful for their children.
ex.zh: 父母总是为子女担忧。

ex.en: Officials are fearful that the epidemic will spread to neighboring provinces.
ex.zh: 官员们担心疫情会蔓延到邻近省份。

ex.en: The storm caused fearful damage to the coastal towns.
ex.zh: 风暴对沿海城镇造成了极其严重的破坏。

senses: adj. 很可怕的,十分吓人的

ex.en: The storm's fearsome winds tore roofs off houses along the entire eastern coastline.
ex.zh: 风暴可怕的大风掀起了整个东部海岸线上房屋的屋顶。

ex.en: Feasibility should be a prime concern in policymaking.
ex.zh: 可行性应该是制定决策时首先要考虑的。

senses: adj. 可行的,合理的,可用的
feasible.usage: [近]practical a. 切实可行的；派生feasibility n.可行性,可能性；feas(做)+ible(形容词后缀)→可以做的→可行的；词根记忆: feas(do, 做)+ible(能…的)→能做的→可行的；索引p408

ex.en: Sounds great but how feasible is this vision?
ex.zh: 听起来很棒，但这一愿景的可行性如何？

ex.en: Changes in the competitive dynamics of this fragmented industry are at last making it feasible for wholesalers to consolidate.
ex.zh: 这种零散型产业的竞争态势中的各种变化终于使批发商联合起来成为可能。

ex.en: Experts doubt whether the plan is technically feasible within five years.
ex.zh: 专家们怀疑该计划在五年内技术上是否可行。

feast.usage: 助记:beast(粗野的人)在feast(节日)里朋友least(最少)

ex.en: The harvest feast was once a way for villagers to thank each other for shared labour.
ex.zh: 丰收宴席曾是村民们为彼此的共同劳动表达感谢的一种方式。

senses: adj. 灵巧的,漂亮的;整洁的;合适的
feat.usage: 助记:neat(细心的)姑娘是很feat(漂亮的)；索引p408

ex.en: Completing the bridge ahead of schedule was an engineering feat few had believed possible.
ex.zh: 提前建成这座桥是一项很少有人认为可能实现的工程壮举。

feather.usage: [构]feather（羽毛）→轻；助记:leather(皮革)上的feather(羽毛)能预测weather(天气);词组feather your own nest中饱私囊

ex.en: The museum displays a rare feather from a bird species thought to have died out a century ago.
ex.zh: 博物馆展出了一根稀有羽毛，来自一种被认为在一个世纪前就已灭绝的鸟类。

feature.usage: [近]characteristic n. 特点；辨析：feature 引人注目的特征；characteristic 突出稳定持久的特性；trait 性格品质的显著特色；vt.以…为特色例为2006年阅读；索引p408

ex.en: Teamwork is a key feature of the training programme.
ex.zh: 团队合作是这项训练计划的重要特点。

ex.en: Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes.
ex.zh: 我们的杂志以满面春风的名人和住在完美住宅中的幸福家庭为特色。

ex.en: The new phone features a camera that works well in low light.
ex.zh: 这款新手机的特色是配备了一枚在弱光下也表现出色的摄像头。

ex.en: Applications submitted before 1 Feb will be processed free of charge, the agency announced.
ex.zh: 该机构宣布，2 月 1 日前提交的申请将免费办理。

ex.en: Retail sales figures released in February revealed a sharp decline in consumer confidence.
ex.zh: 二月发布的零售数据揭示了消费者信心的大幅下滑。

ex.en: In 'federal' and 'confederation', the root 'feder-' carries the idea of a league or treaty.
ex.zh: 在 federal 和 confederation 中，词根 feder- 含有联盟或契约之意。

federal.usage: [族]federation n. 联邦；派生 federalism n. 联邦主义；federalist n. 联邦主义者；联想记忆：fed(看成friend,朋友)+eral(形容词后缀)→国家结成朋友般牢固关系的→联邦的；真题搭配：federal immigration law 联邦移民法；federal stat

ex.en: Federal law requires employers to pay a minimum hourly wage.
ex.zh: 联邦法律要求雇主支付每小时最低工资。

ex.en: The project received two million dollars in federal funding.
ex.zh: 该项目获得了两百万美元的联邦拨款。

ex.en: The country moved from a loose confederation to a federal system.
ex.zh: 该国从松散的邦联转变为联邦制。

senses: n. 同盟，联邦，联盟，联邦政府

ex.en: The trade federation negotiates on behalf of members whose businesses span several neighbouring countries.
ex.zh: 该贸易联合会代表其业务横跨多个邻国的成员进行谈判。

fee.usage: [近]charge n. 费用；助记:音"费"→学费;a license fee执照费;tuition fees学费

ex.en: Another factor may be that more people are trying to overpack their carry-on bags to avoid checked-baggage fees, though the airlines strongly dispute this.
ex.zh: 另一因素可能是越来越多的乘客为了避免支付托运行李费用,过度打包随身携带行李,而航空公司极力反对这一点。

ex.en: This keeps fees high and innovation slow.
ex.zh: 这使得收费居高不下且创新缓慢。

ex.en: Universities are raising tuition fees to cover the cost of teaching.
ex.zh: 大学正在提高学费以支付教学成本。

ex.en: The lawyer charges a fixed fee for an initial consultation.
ex.zh: 这位律师对初次咨询收取固定费用。

senses: adj. 虚弱的，衰弱的；无效的；无力的
feeble.usage: 反义strong adj.强壮的;派生feebly adv.虚弱地;feebleness n.虚弱,软弱;无效；虚弱的（feeble）人应该吃一些有营养的食物（food）。；索引p408

ex.en: She made a feeble attempt to explain what had happened.
ex.zh: 她无力地试图解释发生的事情。

ex.en: Bosses and boards have finally sorted out their worst accounting and compliance troubles, and improved their feeble corporation governance.
ex.zh: 老板们和董事会们终于解决了最糟糕的财务和合规的问题，并加强了原本薄弱的企业管理。

ex.en: The committee offered only a feeble excuse for delaying the reform.
ex.zh: 对于推迟改革，委员会只给出了一个站不住脚的借口。

senses: vt. 喂养；饲养；养；灌输；供应
feed.usage: be fed up with...对……感到厌烦；另 feed up 养肥，养壮；feed back 反馈，反应

ex.en: Farmers feed corn and soybeans to their pigs.
ex.zh: 农民用玉米和大豆喂猪。

ex.en: The children fed the ducks by the lake on Sunday afternoon.
ex.zh: 星期天下午，孩子们在湖边喂鸭子。

ex.en: This data feed updates the website's figures every hour.
ex.zh: 该数据源每小时更新网站上的数字。

senses: n. 反馈的意见（或信息）
feedback.usage: n.反馈；feed（提供）+back（回来）→提供给你的信息，你需要看后返回来→反馈；索引p408

ex.en: If you're not sure, ask for honest feedback from trusted friends, colleagues and professionals.
ex.zh: 如果你不确定，向你信任的朋友、同事和专业人士寻求诚实的反馈。

ex.en: The teacher gave each student detailed feedback on their essay.
ex.zh: 老师对每个学生的文章都给出了详细的反馈。

ex.en: Customer feedback plays a vital role in improving products and services.
ex.zh: 客户反馈对改进产品和服务起着至关重要的作用。

senses: vi. 摸起来有某种感觉
feel.usage: feel like doing sth.想要做某事

ex.en: Many unemployed workers feel that retraining programmes rarely lead to the jobs they were promised.
ex.zh: 许多失业者感到再培训项目很少能带来当初承诺的工作。

feeling.usage: [构]feel的名词形式；辨析：feeling 指因外界刺激表现出的心理状态或生理感觉；emotion 指强烈动人的情绪(喜、怒、哀、乐等)

ex.en: Her feeling of isolation eased once she joined a local book club in her neighbourhood.
ex.zh: 自从加入社区的读书俱乐部后，她的孤独感有所缓解。

ex.en: Her fellow researchers initially dismissed the findings, but later experiments confirmed them beyond doubt.
ex.zh: 她的研究同伴起初对这些发现不以为然，但后来的实验无疑证实了它们。

ex.en: She was awarded a research fellowship that allowed her to spend two years at an American university.
ex.zh: 她获得了一项研究奖学金，得以在一所美国大学从事两年的研究。

ex.en: The study found that female applicants were 30 percent less likely to be invited for interviews.
ex.zh: 研究发现，女性申请者获得面试邀请的可能性要低百分之三十。

senses: adj. 女性的,有女性气质的
feminine.usage: 辨析:feminine指女性特点;female指生物的性别

ex.en: Advertising often links the product to traditionally feminine qualities, a strategy critics consider outdated.
ex.zh: 广告常常把产品与传统的女性气质联系起来，批评者认为这种策略已经过时。

ex.en: The nineteenth-century feminist argued that women's education was essential to the progress of society as a whole.
ex.zh: 这位十九世纪的女权主义者主张，女性教育对整个社会的进步至关重要。

fence.usage: sit on the fence保持中立；观望

ex.en: The farmers argued over a fence that had stood between their properties for over a century.
ex.zh: 农夫们为一道在他们地产之间矗立了一个多世纪的栅栏争论不休。

senses: v. 照料;保护;抵挡;击退

ex.en: Left to fend for themselves after their parents' death, the brothers quickly learned to manage the farm.
ex.zh: 父母去世后兄弟俩只能自谋生计，他们很快学会了经营农场。

ex.en: The defenders managed to fend off repeated attacks until reinforcements finally arrived.
ex.zh: 防守者奋力抵挡住了一波又一波的攻击，直到援军最终赶到。

ex.en: In 'transfer' and 'refer', the root 'fer-' carries the basic sense of bringing or carrying.
ex.zh: 在 transfer 和 refer 中，词根 fer- 含有“带来、拿取”的基本意义。

ex.en: A new ferry service now connects the island to the mainland twice a day during summer.
ex.zh: 现在夏季每天有两班新的渡船服务连接该岛与大陆。

senses: adj. 肥沃的；能生育的；可繁殖的；能结果的
fertile.usage: 派生 fertility n. 肥沃；多产；丰富；fert（发音类似fat“肥的”）+ile（联想成Nile“尼罗河”）→尼罗河孕育着“肥沃的”土地。

ex.en: Farmers worked in the fertile valleys.
ex.zh: 农民们在肥沃的山谷里耕种。

ex.en: The fertile soil of the valley supports a wide range of crops.
ex.zh: 山谷肥沃的土壤适宜种植多种作物。

ex.en: The region proved fertile ground for new technology companies.
ex.zh: 事实证明，该地区是孕育新科技公司的沃土。

ex.en: A healthy diet helps couples remain fertile for longer.
ex.zh: 健康饮食有助于夫妇保持更长时间的生育能力。

ex.en: Excessive use of chemical fertiliser has polluted many rivers that once supported rich wildlife.
ex.zh: 化肥的过度使用污染了许多曾经滋养着丰富野生动植物的河流。

senses: n. [U] 富饶；丰产；想象力丰富

ex.en: Modern irrigation turned the desert region into farmland of remarkable fertility.
ex.zh: 现代灌溉技术使这片沙漠地区变成了异常肥沃的农田。

ex.en: Bees fertilize flowers as they move from plant to plant collecting nectar.
ex.zh: 蜜蜂在植物间穿梭采集花蜜时，便为花朵授了粉。

ex.en: Too much fertilizer washes into rivers and kills aquatic life.
ex.zh: 过量化肥流入河流，导致水生生物死亡。

ex.en: The farmers spread fertilizer on the fields before the spring planting.
ex.zh: 农民在春播前把肥料撒到田里。

ex.en: Organic fertilizer improves the soil instead of exhausting it.
ex.zh: 有机肥能改良土壤，而不是耗尽地力。

ex.en: Farmers were advised to apply fertilizer in spring, when crops can absorb nutrients most efficiently.
ex.zh: 专家建议农民在春季施肥，因为此时作物吸收养分的效率最高。

ex.en: The town's annual music festival generates income for hotels and restaurants far beyond the summer months.
ex.zh: 该镇一年一度的音乐节为酒店和餐厅带来的收入远远超出夏季这几个月。

ex.en: The streets took on a festive air as stalls, lanterns and music appeared ahead of the holiday.
ex.zh: 节日来临前，街边出现了货摊、灯笼和音乐，街道呈现出节日的气氛。

ex.en: The auction is expected to fetch more than two million pounds for the Victorian painting.
ex.zh: 这幅维多利亚时期的画作预计将在拍卖会上拍出两百多万英镑。

ex.en: Under the feudal system, peasants worked land owned by lords in return for protection.
ex.zh: 在封建制度下，农民耕种领主的土地，以此换取保护。

senses: n. 封建主义；封建制度

ex.en: The rise of trade in the fifteenth century slowly undermined the economic foundations of feudalism.
ex.zh: 十五世纪贸易的兴起逐渐动摇了封建主义的经济基础。

ex.en: The discovery of gold sent a fever of speculation through the small mining town.
ex.zh: 金矿的发现在这座小镇掀起了一股投机狂热。

senses: a. 发烧的；发烧引起的；激动的；焦虑不安的
adj. 激动的,焦虑不安的;发烧的,发烧引起的

ex.en: The child felt feverish and was sent home from school.
ex.zh: 孩子感到发烧，被学校送回了家。

ex.en: Reporters worked at a feverish pace to cover the election.
ex.zh: 记者们以狂热的节奏报道选举。

ex.en: She grew feverish after the operation and was kept in hospital.
ex.zh: 她术后开始发烧，因此被留在医院观察。

ex.en: Few of the students who signed up for the course realised how much fieldwork it required.
ex.zh: 报名这门课程的学生中很少有人意识到它需要多少实地调查。

ex.en: Doctors recommend a diet rich in fibre to lower the risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 医生建议食用富含纤维的饮食，以降低患心脏病的风险。

ex.en: In 'fibre' and 'fibrous', the root 'fibr-' refers to thread-like structures.
ex.zh: 在 fibre 和 fibrous 中，词根 fibr- 指丝状、纤维状的结构。

senses: n. [C,U] (织物或绳等的)纤维制品
n. [C] (人或动物身体组织的)纤维
fibre.usage: 记 fibr(纤维)+e→纤维；亦作 fiber

ex.en: Optical fibres carry information as pulses of light, far faster than copper cables.
ex.zh: 光纤以光脉冲的形式传输信息，速度远快于铜缆。

ex.en: In 'factory', 'benefit' and 'facility', the root 'fic/fact/facil' carries the sense of doing or making.
ex.zh: 在 factory、benefit 和 facility 中，词根 fic/fact/facil 含有“做、制作”之意。

ex.en: In verbs such as 'certify', the ending '-ficate' marks an action rather than a thing.
ex.zh: 在 certify 这类动词中，词尾 -ficate 表示动作而非事物。

ex.en: The ending '-fication' turns verbs into nouns, as in 'simplification' and 'certification'.
ex.zh: 词尾 -fication 把动词变成名词，如 simplification 和 certification。

fiction.usage: 30 "fiction"相关词汇；发音类似"飞可神"→想象一个画面，每个人都像神一样飞起来了，现实生活中不会发生吧，这应该是在"小说"里；词根记忆：fict(make,制作)+ion(名词后缀)→作家制作的→小说。；索引p408

ex.en: Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace.
ex.zh: 生于数字时代的年轻人确实变得越来越擅长辨别网络世界中的真假消息。

ex.en: The boundary between fiction and reality blurs in his early novels.
ex.zh: 在他早期的小说中，虚构与现实的界限是模糊的。

ex.en: science fiction
ex.zh: 科幻小说

ex.en: In 'confide' and 'fidelity', the root 'fid-' expresses trust or belief.
ex.zh: 在 confide 和 fidelity 中，词根 fid- 表示信任或相信。

senses: n. 领域,范围;(电磁等)场

ex.en: Her field of research, behavioural economics, was once dismissed as a passing fashion.
ex.zh: 她的研究领域——行为经济学，曾一度被视为昙花一现的时髦学问而不被重视。

ex.en: In 'feral' and 'ferocious', the element 'fier/fer-' describes something wild or untamed.
ex.zh: 在 feral 和 ferocious 中，成分 fier/fer- 表示野生的、未驯化的。

senses: adj. 凶猛的；强烈的，猛烈的；狂暴的；狂热的
fierce.usage: 记 fier(野生的)+ce→野生动物大多是凶悍的→凶猛的；近 intense a. 激烈的；派生:fiercely adv.凶猛地;fierceness n.凶猛；adj.强烈的，激烈的；凶猛的；发音类似"飞蛾死"→飞蛾扑火而死→扑火很激烈→狂热的

ex.en: Any threat of monopoly, they argue, is removed by fierce competition from trucks.
ex.zh: 他们认为，在公路运输的激烈竞争面前，垄断的威胁已经不复存在。

ex.en: The two companies are engaged in fierce competition for the young market.
ex.zh: 这两家公司正在为争夺年轻人市场展开激烈竞争。

ex.en: Fierce storms destroyed much of the winter wheat in the region.
ex.zh: 狂风暴雨摧毁了该地区的大量冬小麦。

ex.en: The chimney was smoking fiercely.
ex.zh: 烟囱猛烈地冒着烟。

ex.en: The bridge, completed fifteen years behind schedule, had already cost twice its original budget.
ex.zh: 这座大桥延期十五年才完工，花费已是原预算的两倍。

ex.en: More than fifty per cent of the respondents said they would pay extra for environmentally friendly products.
ex.zh: 超过百分之五十的受访者表示，愿意为环保产品支付额外费用。

ex.en: Local residents continue to fight plans for a motorway that would cut through ancient woodland.
ex.zh: 当地居民继续反对修建一条将穿过古老林地的高速公路的计划。

figure.usage: ① n.（尤指官方资料中的）数字；② v. 弄清楚（2017年阅读）：Taking a gap year to figure things out；索引p408

ex.en: It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling.
ex.zh: 它特别容易受到光照的损坏,到了九十年代中期,Gilardi的南瓜、玫瑰和其他塑像都出现了裂缝和碎屑。

ex.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
ex.zh: 那些数字有很多值得注意的地方，但它们（所代表的问题）仍然很严峻。

ex.en: Official figures show that unemployment has fallen for six months in a row.
ex.zh: 官方数字显示失业率已连续六个月下降。

ex.en: She does yoga three times a week to keep her figure.
ex.zh: 她每周做三次瑜伽以保持身材。

senses: vt.&vi. 送交(备案)；提出(申请)
n. [C] (计算机的)文件；卷宗；文件夹
file.usage: 记 fil(线)+e→用线装订的记录案件的文字材料→卷宗；近 submit；document；索引p408

ex.en: Please file the reports alphabetically by author's name.
ex.zh: 请按作者姓名的字母顺序将这些报告归档。

ex.en: The company filed for bankruptcy after failing to repay its debts.
ex.zh: 该公司因无力偿还债务而申请破产。

ex.en: I cannot find the file you sent me this morning.
ex.zh: 我找不到你今天上午发给我的那份文件。

senses: n. [C] 文件编档员；文件装订员；锉磨工人

ex.en: The court's online system allows any filer to submit documents without visiting the clerk's office.
ex.zh: 法院的在线系统使任何提起诉讼者都能提交文件而无需前往书记员办公室。

senses: n. 存档,归档;存档档案,归档记录;锉刀

ex.en: The company's filing with the regulator revealed losses that had been hidden from investors.
ex.zh: 该公司向监管机构提交的存档文件披露了曾向投资者隐瞒的亏损。

ex.en: The company cannot fill skilled positions because too few graduates possess the required technical training.
ex.zh: 这家公司无法填补技术岗位空缺，因为具备所需技术训练的毕业生太少。

ex.en: The director chose to film the entire documentary in black and white to evoke an earlier era.
ex.zh: 导演选择用黑白拍摄整部纪录片，以唤起对更早时代的回忆。

senses: n. [U] 电影摄制，电影制片

ex.en: Digital technology has transformed film-making, putting powerful tools within reach of ordinary creators.
ex.zh: 数字技术改变了电影制作，让普通人也能拥有强大的创作工具。

ex.en: Readers must filter the constant stream of online information, separating reliable sources from mere noise.
ex.zh: 读者必须过滤源源不断的网络信息，把可靠的来源与纯粹的噪音区分开来。

final.usage: adj.最终的；决定性的 n.决赛；期末考试，课程终结考 试 很小dose 的heroin 就可以改变人体的hormone 分泌，让人们感觉游走在heaven 和地狱之间，让幻觉不 停flash,所以专家给出counsel，要全面禁止毒品，

ex.en: The final decision rests with the board of directors.
ex.zh: 最终决定权在董事会手中。

ex.en: The two best teams will meet in the final next Saturday.
ex.zh: 两支最强的球队将于下周六在决赛中相遇。

ex.en: The final chapter of the book offers a possible solution to the crisis.
ex.zh: 本书的最后一章为这场危机提供了一个可能的解决方案。

senses: vt. 最终确定(计划、协议等)

ex.en: Negotiators hoped to finalise the trade agreement before the end of the year.
ex.zh: 谈判代表希望能在年底前最终敲定这项贸易协定。

senses: adv. (用于列举、引出观点等)最后

ex.en: After years of debate, the council finally approved funding for the long-delayed cycle network.
ex.zh: 经过多年辩论，市议会终于批准了为拖延已久的自行车路网提供资金。

senses: n. 财政,金融;财务状况
n. 财政；金融；资金；财务
finance.usage: n.财政，金融；资金；经济情况 v.提供资金；n.财政，金融；资金；经济情况 v.提供资金；资助；n.财政，金融；资金；财务情 况 v.提供资金；资助；发音类似"犯难死"→当西方发生"金融"危机时，很多人都会犯难→金融，财政，资金；financial adj. 财政的，金融的；finances 资金。；索引p408

ex.en: She developed a strong interest in finance.
ex.zh: 她对金融产生了浓厚的兴趣。

ex.en: The project is partly financed by the government.
ex.zh: 该项目部分由政府出资。

ex.en: He works in finance.
ex.zh: 他在金融行业工作。

ex.en: For someone moving from finance to advertising, maybe they want to look more "SoHo."
ex.zh: 对于从金融圈跳槽到广告界的人来说，也许他们希望自己看上去更前卫。

ex.en: But Congress should look into doing so directly, by helping to finance PreCheck enrollment or to cut costs in other ways.
ex.zh: 但是美国国会应该直接介入这种做法，通过向预检注册提供资金或削减其他方面的开支来提供帮助。

senses: adj. 财政的，财务的，金融的
financial.usage: (词频45)；adj.财政的，金融的；拓展：financial products 金融产品；索引p408

ex.en: financial constraints // financial crisis
ex.zh: 财务限制 // 金融危机

ex.en: The university offers financial support to students from low-income families.
ex.zh: 这所大学为低收入家庭的学生提供经济资助。

ex.en: Many small businesses collapsed during the global financial crisis of 2008.
ex.zh: 许多小企业在2008年全球金融危机期间倒闭了。

ex.en: Many students depend financially on their parents, at least during the first years of university.
ex.zh: 许多学生在经济上依赖父母，至少在大学的头几年是如此。

senses: n. 发现物，被发现的人
find.usage: v.找到，找回；发现 n.被发现的人，发现物

ex.en: Scientists found traces of water in the soil samples brought back from Mars.
ex.zh: 科学家在从火星带回的土壤样本中发现了水的痕迹。

ex.en: She found it difficult to concentrate with the radio on.
ex.zh: 她发现开着收音机很难集中注意力。

ex.en: Among the museum's recent finds is a Roman coin almost untouched by time.
ex.zh: 博物馆近期的发现物中有一枚几乎未受岁月侵蚀的罗马钱币。

finding.usage: n.发现物，研究结果，调查（或 研究）的结果

ex.en: The report's central finding contradicts the widely held belief that class sizes determine educational quality.
ex.zh: 该报告的核心调查结果与班级规模决定教育质量这一普遍看法相矛盾。

senses: a. 好的；晴朗的；细小的
a. 高质量的；健康的；漂亮的；精美的；晴朗的
fine.usage: 派生finely美好地,准确地;fineness精巧;finable应罚款的

ex.en: Companies that breach data-protection rules may face a fine of up to four percent of global turnover.
ex.zh: 违反数据保护规定的公司可能面临最高达全球营业额百分之四的罚款。

ex.en: Cabinet-makers prize fine-grained wood because it can be polished to an exceptionally smooth surface.
ex.zh: 细木工匠青睐纹理细密的木材，因为它可以被打磨得异常光滑。

ex.en: The evidence points the finger at poor maintenance rather than operator error for the accident.
ex.zh: 证据表明这起事故的罪魁祸首是维护不善，而非操作失误。

senses: n. 结尾,末尾,最后阶段

ex.en: The runners were granted extra time to finish the marathon after the storm interrupted the start.
ex.zh: 由于暴雨中断了起跑，跑者们获准延长完成马拉松的时间。

senses: adj. 有限的，有限制的；限定的
finite.usage: 同义:limited;反义:infinite无限的；adj.有限的 n.有限之物；adj.有限的，有限制的；索引p408

ex.en: Fossil fuels exist in finite quantities and will one day run out.
ex.zh: 化石燃料储量有限，总有一天会耗尽。

ex.en: Human memory is finite, so we rely on notes and records.
ex.zh: 人的记忆力是有限的，所以我们依靠笔记和记录。

ex.en: The planet's resources are finite and must be managed with care.
ex.zh: 地球资源是有限的，必须谨慎管理。

books.unit: 附录 I 部分国家(或地区)名称及相关信息

ex.en: Finland's schools consistently rank among the world's best, despite assigning relatively little homework.
ex.zh: 尽管布置的家庭作业相对较少，芬兰的学校却始终位居世界前列。

senses: n. [U] 火；[U,C] 火灾；[C] 炉火
n. 火;热情,激情;射击,火力

ex.en: The factory fire destroyed equipment worth millions and left hundreds of workers temporarily unemployed.
ex.zh: 工厂大火烧毁了价值数百万的设备，并使数百名工人暂时失业。

ex.en: The festival began with a string of firecrackers which, by tradition, were meant to drive away bad luck.
ex.zh: 庆典以一挂鞭炮开场，按照传统，鞭炮是用来驱走霉运的。

senses: n. 消防队员;司炉工,烧火工人
fireman.usage: 助记:fire(火)+man(男人)→灭火的男人→消防队员

ex.en: The fireman carried the old man down three flights of smoky stairs to safety.
ex.zh: 消防队员抱着老人穿过三层烟雾弥漫的楼梯，把他带到安全地带。

fireplace.usage: 助记:fire(火)+place(地点,场所)→烧火的地点→壁炉

ex.en: The family gathered around the fireplace, roasting chestnuts and telling stories far into the night.
ex.zh: 一家人围坐在壁炉旁，烤着栗子讲故事，直到深夜。

ex.en: The city cancelled its New Year fireworks because of fears that sparks could start wildfires.
ex.zh: 由于担心火星引发野火，该市取消了新年烟花表演。

senses: adj. 坚固的;坚决的,坚定的
firm.usage: n.公司，商行 adj.结实的，坚硬的；牢固的 v.使强壮，使坚实；索引p408

ex.en: The law firm hired twenty new graduates this autumn.
ex.zh: 这家律师事务所今年秋天招聘了二十名应届毕业生。

ex.en: She remained firm in her opposition to the merger despite heavy pressure.
ex.zh: 尽管压力很大，她仍坚决反对这次合并。

ex.en: Firm action is needed to stop companies from dumping waste into rivers.
ex.zh: 需要采取坚决的行动来阻止企业向河流倾倒废物。

firmly.usage: adv.坚固地，牢固地；坚决地；adv.坚固地，牢固地

ex.en: The minister firmly rejected suggestions that the reform had been rushed through parliament.
ex.zh: 部长坚决否认有关该改革草率通过议会的说法。

senses: adj. 第一的,最重要的,首要的;最优秀的
adv. 首先,第一,最初;(强调不愿)宁可
first.usage: first and last 从各方面看,完全地

ex.en: The first survey of the reef revealed damage far more extensive than scientists had predicted.
ex.zh: 对珊瑚礁的首次调查所揭示的损害远比科学家预测的严重。

senses: adj. 财政的;国库的;国家岁入的
fiscal.usage: monetary policy 货币政策（对比记忆）；索引p408

ex.en: It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue.
ex.zh: 它(指美国邮政署)报告称2016财年净损失额达56亿美元，连续十年入不敷出。

ex.en: The government tightened fiscal policy to curb rising inflation.
ex.zh: 政府收紧财政政策以遏制不断上升的通货膨胀。

ex.en: The fiscal year ends in March, when departments settle their accounts.
ex.zh: 财政年度于三月结束，各部门届时结清账目。

ex.en: Critics say the fiscal stimulus mainly benefited large corporations.
ex.zh: 批评者说财政刺激主要让大公司受益。

ex.en: Overfishing has caused stocks of large fish to fall sharply across the world's oceans.
ex.zh: 过度捕捞已导致全球海洋中大型鱼类的数量急剧下降。

ex.en: Every fisherman in the village now carries a device that reports catches to the coastal authority.
ex.zh: 村里的每位渔民现在都携带一个向海岸管理部门报告渔获量的设备。

ex.en: Strict quotas were introduced to save the cod fishery from total collapse.
ex.zh: 政府实行严格的配额制度，以拯救鳕鱼渔场免于彻底崩溃。

ex.en: Bans on fishing during the breeding season have allowed fish stocks to recover remarkably quickly.
ex.zh: 繁殖季节的捕鱼禁令使鱼类资源得到了显著的恢复。

ex.en: She clenched her fist as the committee announced that her proposal had been rejected again.
ex.zh: 当委员会宣布她的提案再次被否决时，她攥紧了拳头。

ex.en: If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus.
ex.zh: 如果你已经知道自己的专业，那么参加与该专业相符的课外活动会是一个很大的加分项。

ex.en: Regular exercise keeps her fit despite her busy schedule.
ex.zh: 尽管日程繁忙，经常锻炼使她保持健康。

ex.en: The new manager is not fit for such a demanding post.
ex.zh: 新任经理不适合担任如此艰巨的职务。

ex.en: Engineers fitted a new cooling system into the old building.
ex.zh: 工程师们给这座老楼安装了新的冷却系统。

senses: n. 健康,健壮;适当,适合

ex.en: I've also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, because I'm training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.
ex.zh: 在实现具体健身目标方面，我也经历了更大的成功，因为我是按照那些目标而不是秤上的数字来训练的。

ex.en: The committee gave the plan five months to prove itself before reviewing the funding.
ex.zh: 委员会给了该计划五个月的验证期，之后将重新审议拨款。

senses: vt. 使固定；修理；修复；安装；确定

ex.en: Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
ex.zh: 欧元区各经济体，无论其经济实力如何，总有一天会因使用单一货币而走向联合，这种货币制度使竞争力不足的成员国无法采取货币贬值这一权宜之计，但是现在市场已经对此失去了信心。

ex.en: The mechanic fixed the leaking pipe within an hour.
ex.zh: 机修工一小时内修好了漏水的管子。

ex.en: They fixed the meeting for the first Monday of each month.
ex.zh: 他们把会议定在每月的第一个星期一。

ex.en: He fixed a shelf to the wall with two screws.
ex.zh: 他用两颗螺丝把架子固定在墙上。
